questions.q: What is the programme mainly about?
options: How to keep cool in hot weather without air conditioning
Why people buy bottled water when tap water is free
Which fizzy drinks are the healthiest for children
How plastic bottles are collected and recycled
questions.why: Rob asks why people don't just drink tap water, and they discuss bottled water and its marketing.

questions.q: Why does Neil say he prefers his bottled water?
options: It is cheaper than other drinks
It is colder than tap water
It has added salts and minerals and tastes better
It comes in a bottle that can be reused
questions.why: Neil says it's enriched with salts and minerals and 'tastes better'.

questions.q: What change in the UK does Neil mention?
options: Bottled water is now more popular than cola
People now drink more tap water than before
Cola sales have doubled
Supermarkets have stopped selling bottled water
questions.why: He says 'for the first time in the UK, bottled water is more popular than cola'.

questions.q: What does Natalie Fee's organisation, City to Sea, campaign against?
options: Fizzy drinks
Dirty tap water
Expensive supermarkets
Plastic pollution
questions.why: Rob says City to Sea campaigns against plastic pollution, which bottled water causes a lot of.

questions.q: According to Natalie Fee, what did bottled water companies do?
options: Made tap water cleaner by paying for new pipes
Spent millions on adverts making people fear tap water
Lowered their prices to beat cola and other fizzy drinks
Paid for taste tests in schools to attract children
questions.why: She says they spent millions on adverts 'scaring us off of tap water'.

questions.q: What does Natalie Fee say about tap water?
options: It's better controlled than bottled water and wins taste tests
It is less healthy than bottled water because of chemicals
It needs added minerals to be as good as bottled water
It tastes worse than bottled water, but it is much cheaper
questions.why: She says tap water is more regulated and 'comes up trumps' in taste tests most times.

questions.q: What does Rob mean when he says 'As cheap as that?' about the £80 iceberg water?
options: He thinks it is a good price
He wants to buy some for Neil
He thinks Neil has got the price wrong
He is joking, because it is very expensive
questions.why: Rob is being sarcastic; £80 a bottle is a very high price for water.

questions.q: What happens in the taste test at the end?
options: Neil can't tell the two waters apart and gives up
Rob prefers the bottled water because it tastes softer
Neil says the tap water tastes better without knowing it
Neil refuses to try the tap water from the kitchen
questions.why: Neil says the second one tastes 'definitely' better, and Rob reveals it's the tap water.
